title: Station Master CBT · Challenge drill
provenance: Original GateLabs questions informed by the published exam pattern. Pattern reference: https://rrb.indianrailways.gov.in/-/image/1793016771817CEN_08_2026_StationMaster.pdf/examsDocuments
note: Original multi-step questions across all four published CBT blocks at the same pace per question as the full CBT. The difficulty label describes the question design.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A 180 m train overtakes a 120 m train moving at 36 km/h in 30 seconds. How long will the faster train take to clear a 270 m platform?
questions.explanation: Relative speed is 300/30 = 10 m/s. Adding 36 km/h = 10 m/s gives 20 m/s. Clearing the platform requires 450/20 = 22.5 s.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A 12 V ideal source feeds a 3 Ω resistor in series with a parallel pair of 6 Ω and 3 Ω resistors. What is the power in the 6 Ω resistor?
questions.explanation: The parallel resistance is 2 Ω, so total current is 2.4 A. The parallel voltage is 4.8 V and power in 6 Ω is 4.8²/6 = 3.84 W.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: P and Q can finish a job in 12 and 18 days respectively. They work together for 4 days. Q leaves and R joins P. They finish the remaining work in 4 days. How many days would R take alone?
questions.explanation: The first pair completes 5/9 of the job. To finish 4/9 in 4 days, P and R need rate 1/9. Subtracting P’s 1/12 leaves R at 1/36.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A 30 kg crate is pulled along a level floor at 2 m/s. The kinetic friction coefficient is 0.25. A second horizontal force of 15 N opposes the motion. With g = 10 m/s², what is the pulling power at constant speed?
questions.explanation: Friction is 0.25 × 300 = 75 N. Add the opposing 15 N, then multiply the required 90 N pull by 2 m/s.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A hollow metal cylinder is 14 cm tall with outer radius 5 cm and inner radius 3 cm. Its mass is 4.928 kg. Using π = 22/7, what is the density of the metal?
questions.explanation: The metal volume is (25−9) × 14 × 22/7 = 704 cm³. The ratio 4928/704 is 7.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: An insulated calorimeter initially at 20°C has the same heat capacity as 100 g of water. It contains 200 g of water at 20°C. A further 200 g of water at 80°C is added. Ignore evaporation. What is the final equilibrium temperature?
questions.explanation: The effective cold mass is 300 g, with 200 g of hot water. Heat balance gives 300(T−20) = 200(80−T), so T = 44°C.

questions.subject: Data Analysis
questions.question: If departures from C double while each station’s on-time rate stays fixed, what is the new network on-time percentage?
questions.explanation: The new on-time count is 108+136+156 = 400 of 120+160+220 = 500 departures.

questions.subject: Data Analysis
questions.question: P and Q together sold 360 tickets across two shifts. Did P sell more tickets than Q overall? I. P sold 40 more than Q in the first shift. II. In the second shift, Q sold 32 more than P.
questions.explanation: Overall P−Q is the sum of the shift differences. With both statements that sum is 40−32 = 8. Either shift alone leaves the other difference unknown.

questions.subject: Data Analysis
questions.question: Among 120 staff, 63 took A, 49 took B and 42 took C. Pair overlaps including the triple are 28 for A/B, 21 for B/C and 18 for A/C. Fifteen took none. How many took exactly two?
questions.explanation: The union is 105; adding singles and subtracting pairs gives 87, so the triple is 18. Exactly two is 67−3×18 = 13.

questions.subject: Data Analysis
questions.question: In which month did the percentage of delayed trips fall most relative to the immediately preceding month, measured in percentage points?
questions.explanation: The delay rates are 15%, 10%, 12%, 6% and 5%. April’s reduction of 6 percentage points is largest.

questions.subject: Data Analysis
questions.question: For the six observations shown, remove the point with highest traffic. What is the median delay of the remaining observations?
questions.explanation: The largest traffic value 36 has delay 15. The others sorted are 5, 6, 8, 9, 12, with median 8.

questions.subject: Data Analysis
questions.question: The delay distribution below excludes ten late-arriving reports. When all reports are included, the mean delay is 3.2 minutes. What is the mean delay among the ten late reports?
questions.explanation: The 50 included reports total 148 delay minutes. All 60 total 3.2 × 60 = 192 minutes. The omitted ten therefore total 44 minutes and average 4.4.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: Which new fact most directly weakens the conclusion that the display itself reduced missed transfers?
options: The comparison stations started unusually low
The display used two smaller screens at each station
The upgraded stations also lengthened connection gaps on the same day
questions.explanation: Longer connection gaps are a separate plausible cause that changed exactly where and when the display changed.
questions.passage: After an electronic display was introduced at several stations, missed transfers fell at those stations. During the same period, missed transfers were stable at stations without the display. The authority concluded that the display itself caused the reduction.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: Every express service uses a numbered platform. No maintenance service uses a numbered platform. Some booked services are maintenance services. Which conclusion must follow?
options: Some booked services are not express services
All booked services are express services
Some numbered-platform services are maintenance services
No booked service uses a numbered platform
questions.explanation: The booked maintenance services cannot use numbered platforms; hence none of those services is express. Other booked services are unrestricted.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: At what time between 7:00 and 8:00 are the two clock hands exactly opposite?
questions.explanation: At 7:00 the hour hand is 210° ahead. The minute hand gains 5.5° per minute. Reducing the lead by 30° takes 60/11 min = 5 5/11 min.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: Exactly one of A, B and C moved a token. A says “B moved it.” B says “C moved it.” C says “B’s statement is false.” Exactly two statements are true. Who moved it?
questions.explanation: B and C make complementary claims, so exactly one of them is true. To have two true statements, A is also true and B moved it.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: Complete the series AZ, CX, FU, JQ, OL, …
questions.explanation: First-letter positions increase by 2,3,4,5, then 6 to U. Second-letter positions decrease by 2,3,4,5, then 6 to F.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: Six files A–F are arranged left to right. C is immediately left of F. Exactly one file sits between C and D. A is right of F and immediately left of E. B is left of D. Which file is fourth?
questions.explanation: C must be at most third to leave space for F and A–E. If D is right of C, the only possible A–E pair is at slots 5–6 with C at slot 2, leaving B at slot 1 and D fourth. If D is left of C, it would be first, leaving no slot for B.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: A three-letter word is coded by shifting its first, second and third letters forward by 1, 3 and 5 places respectively, wrapping past Z, then reversing the result. Which word is coded as “CCB”?
questions.explanation: Reverse to BCC. Shift back by 1, 3 and 5 to get A, Z and X.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: Find the next term: 3, 9, 8, 24, 21, 63, 58, …
questions.explanation: The operations alternate multiplying by 3 and subtracting successive odds 1, 3 and 5. The next term is 58×3 = 174.

title: RRB Station Master CBT · Challenge drill 2
note: Original questions modelled on overlapping skills in the 2025 NTPC Graduate CBT papers and the CEN 08/2026 Station Master syllabus. The 20-question drill uses a 6/6/4/4 mix with an answer and explanation for every question.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A supply shop buys a tool for ₹1300. It marks the tool up by 50% and offers a 20% discount on the marked price. How much profit does the shop make on the sale?
questions.explanation: The shop paid ₹1300. It adds half of that price to make the price on the tag. The tag shows 1.5 × ₹1300 = ₹1950. A 20% discount takes away 20 out of every 100 rupees on the tag. The buyer pays the remaining 80%, which is 0.8 × ₹1950 = ₹1560. The shop keeps the amount above what it paid. Subtract the cost from the money received. ₹1560 − ₹1300 = ₹260.

steps: The shop paid ₹1300. It adds half of that price to make the price on the tag. The tag shows 1.5 × ₹1300 = ₹1950.
A 20% discount takes away 20 out of every 100 rupees on the tag. The buyer pays the remaining 80%, which is 0.8 × ₹1950 = ₹1560.
The shop keeps the amount above what it paid. Subtract the cost from the money received. ₹1560 − ₹1300 = ₹260.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A set of 52 freight weights has a mean of 110 kg. One entry was understated by 104 kg and another overstated by 52 kg. What is the corrected average?
questions.explanation: Think of the 52 weights as one pile. To recover the old total, multiply 52 by the old average of 110 kg. That gives 5720 kg. One entry is 104 kg too small, so add 104 kg. Another is 52 kg too big, so take 52 kg away. The new total is 5720 + 104 − 52 = 5772 kg. The number of entries is still 52. Share the new total equally across those entries. 5772 ÷ 52 = 111 kg.

steps: Think of the 52 weights as one pile. To recover the old total, multiply 52 by the old average of 110 kg. That gives 5720 kg.
One entry is 104 kg too small, so add 104 kg. Another is 52 kg too big, so take 52 kg away. The new total is 5720 + 104 − 52 = 5772 kg.
The number of entries is still 52. Share the new total equally across those entries. 5772 ÷ 52 = 111 kg.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A dealer buys two equal-sized batches at the same cost per item. The first batch yields a profit of 92% and the second a loss of 46% on its cost. What is the profit percentage on the total cost?
questions.explanation: Both batches cost the same, so pretend each cost ₹100. The first earns ₹92 extra and the second loses ₹46. Take the loss away from the gain. You keep ₹92 − ₹46 = ₹46 extra. That extra money came from buying both batches for ₹200 altogether. Divide 46 by 200 and multiply by 100 to get 23%.

steps: Both batches cost the same, so pretend each cost ₹100. The first earns ₹92 extra and the second loses ₹46.
Take the loss away from the gain. You keep ₹92 − ₹46 = ₹46 extra.
That extra money came from buying both batches for ₹200 altogether. Divide 46 by 200 and multiply by 100 to get 23%.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A vessel holds 500 cm³ of one liquid and twice that volume of another. Their densities are 1 and 1.3 g/cm³. The volumes add exactly. What is the mixture density?
questions.explanation: Think of the mixture as three cups of 500 cm³ each. One cup is the first liquid and two cups are the second liquid. Each cubic centimetre of the first liquid has a mass of 1 g. Each cubic centimetre of the second has a mass of 1.3 g. Multiply each amount of liquid by its own density. Add those masses and divide by all 1500 cm³. The common cup size cancels, leaving (1 + 2 × 1.3) ÷ 3 = 1.2 g/cm³.

steps: Think of the mixture as three cups of 500 cm³ each. One cup is the first liquid and two cups are the second liquid.
Each cubic centimetre of the first liquid has a mass of 1 g. Each cubic centimetre of the second has a mass of 1.3 g. Multiply each amount of liquid by its own density.
Add those masses and divide by all 1500 cm³. The common cup size cancels, leaving (1 + 2 × 1.3) ÷ 3 = 1.2 g/cm³.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A signal cycles through 46 settings numbered 0 through 45. It starts at setting 44 and advances 2351 times. What setting is displayed?
questions.explanation: 2346 advances form complete cycles. The remaining five advance from 44 through the wrap at zero. The display stops at setting 3.

steps: 2346 advances form complete cycles. The remaining five advance from 44 through the wrap at zero.
The display stops at setting 3.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A stock clerk must split 184 red and 322 blue tags into as many identical packs as possible, using every tag. How many tags go in each pack?
questions.explanation: Every pack must receive the same number of red tags as the other packs. The same is true for blue tags. So the number of packs must divide both 184 and 322 exactly. Write the totals as 4 × 46 and 7 × 46. The 4 and 7 have no common factor bigger than 1, so 46 is the greatest number of packs you can make. Split the red tags across 46 packs to get 4 red tags per pack. Split the blue tags the same way to get 7 blue tags per pack. Add them. 4 + 7 = 11 tags.

steps: Every pack must receive the same number of red tags as the other packs. The same is true for blue tags. So the number of packs must divide both 184 and 322 exactly.
Write the totals as 4 × 46 and 7 × 46. The 4 and 7 have no common factor bigger than 1, so 46 is the greatest number of packs you can make.
Split the red tags across 46 packs to get 4 red tags per pack. Split the blue tags the same way to get 7 blue tags per pack. Add them. 4 + 7 = 11 tags.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: If all four rules are kept, which appointment order is valid?
options: O → T → Y → D → I → N
O → T → D → Y → I → N
O → D → T → Y → I → N
O → T → Y → I → D → N
questions.explanation: The ends and penultimate appointment are fixed. The three remaining slots must contain the pair T–Y followed by D. Read the complete order: O → T → Y → D → I → N.
questions.passage:
Six review appointments O, T, Y, D, I, N run in slots 1–6. Each slot has one appointment.
1. O opens the schedule and N closes it.
2. Y directly follows T.
3. I is immediately before N.
4. D is later than Y.

steps: The ends and penultimate appointment are fixed. The three remaining slots must contain the pair T–Y followed by D.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: The labels on rooms W and L are swapped after placement. Which statement is correct for the resulting layout?
options: G is two floors above W.
Q is on the highest floor.
questions.explanation: Swap only the two named labels. W now appears on floor 5 and L on floor 2. Q was unaffected and remains on floor 6. The statements involving the new W and L positions fail.
questions.passage:
Six archive rooms R, W, B, G, L, Q occupy a building’s six floors, one room per floor. Floor 1 is the lowest.
G is two floors above W.
B is immediately below G.
Q is on the highest floor.
R is below W and L is above G.

steps: Swap only the two named labels. W now appears on floor 5 and L on floor 2.
Q was unaffected and remains on floor 6. The statements involving the new W and L positions fail.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: Which conclusion is true for every allowed alarm combination?
options: Both P and R are inactive.
P and S cannot both be active.
questions.explanation: Check the two cases for the exclusive pair. If P is active, S must be inactive. If R is active, P is inactive and S must be active. These cases force P and S to be incompatible.
questions.passage: The three alarm flags W, B, G are called P, R and S in the statements. Exactly one of P and R is active. If R is active, S is active. If S is active, P is inactive. At least one alarm combination is allowed.

steps: Check the two cases for the exclusive pair. If P is active, S must be inactive. If R is active, P is inactive and S must be active.
These cases force P and S to be incompatible.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: Which comparison best separates those explanations?
options: Compare only the final speeds of those who signed up.
Compare the number of sessions held in different months.
Compare gains after offering the session randomly among trainees with similar baseline speeds.
Compare the earliest signup times with the last finishing times.
questions.explanation: Matching baseline speeds and varying access reduces the role of self-selection in the observed gain.
questions.passage: A coach reported that the quickest trainees all elected to take an extra practice session. The coach wanted to know whether the session improved speed or simply attracted people who were already quick.

questions.explanation: There are three entries with larger scores, even though the middle two share position 2. The next entry therefore receives rank 4.

questions.question: To encode a number, first subtract 47 from 106. Then add either 8 or 11, choosing 8 when the result is even and 11 when it is odd. What final number is produced?
questions.explanation: The initial result is 59. Test that intermediate result for parity. Then apply just the matching offset.
